passages.title: David’s Transfer of the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem.
passages.text: The ark signified the Mosaic covenant. It also symbolized God’s presence on earth. It had been neglected throughout Saul’s reign, being kept in the village of Kiriath-jearim ( 13:3 , 5 ). The Chronicler departs from his source’s order ( 2 Samuel 5–6 ) to present David’s first attempt to retrieve the ark ( 1 Chron. 13:5–14 = 2 Sam. 6:1–11 ); he places this event before David’s establishment of his home and family in Jerusalem and his defeat of the Philistines ( 1 Chron. 14:1–17 = 2 Sam. 5:11–25 ). He changes the order of these events to show that David’s true priority is his commitment to God.

passages.title: 1 Chron 13:1–4
passages.text: David’s consultation shows a concern with national unity and a desire to involve the people in national issues. **we did not seek it**. See “seek my face,” 2 Chron. 7:14 . To “seek” the ark would mean caring for it rightly as the focus of worship. “Seeking God” will emerge as a major theme in Chronicles. During David’s reign there will be an improvement in the people’s commitment to God, compared to their level of commitment during the **days of Saul**.

passages.title: 1 Chron 13:5–6
passages.text: People from all over Israel participated in retrieving the ark: **from the Nile of Egypt to Lebo-hamath** in the far northeast. Compare the boundaries of the Promised Land, Gen. 15:18 . On **who sits enthroned above the cherubim**, see note on 1 Sam. 4:3–4 .

passages.title: 1 Chron 13:7–12
passages.text: The Levites were to carry the ark on poles ( Ex. 25:12–15 ; see note on 2 Sam. 6:3–4 ). Transporting the ark by **cart** ( 1 Chron. 13:7 ), as the Philistines had done ( 1 Samuel 6 ), demonstrated a lack of reverence for the sacred object of God’s presence and for the Law of Moses. **Uzzah** intended well, but he disobeyed the Lord by touching the ark (see Num. 4:15 ; also note on 2 Sam. 6:6–11 ).

passages.title: 1 Chron 13:13–14
passages.text: **Obed-edom** was probably a foreigner, particularly if **Gittite** (a resident of Gath) means that he was a Philistine.

notes.text: On **David . . . celebrating before God** with various instruments, see note on 2 Sam. 6:5 .
